title: Iran closes its airspace by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran initiates a major closure of its airspace, that is not solely due to weather conditions, by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or suspension of commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from Iranian airspace or a major Iranian Airspace region. A qualifying closure must apply generally to flights across Iran or a major Iranian airspace region. Limited cancellations, delays, or other partial closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain flights pre-approved by the Iranian Civil Aviation Authority may be permitted). 

Any non-weather complete suspension of commercial arrivals and departures affecting at least two of the following airports will qualify: Imam Khomeini International Airport (IKA), Mehrabad Airport (THR), Mashhad International Airport (MHD), Shiraz International Airport (SYZ), or Isfahan International Airport (IFN).

Qualifying previous examples include the January 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace except to international flights with express governmental permission (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shuts-airspace-most-flights-flightradar24-says-2026-01-14/) and the April 2024 closure of Iran’s western airspace (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-airports-cancel-flights-until-monday-morning-2024-04-14/). Non-qualifying examples include the January 27, 2026 partial closure of Iranian airspace around the Strait of Hormuz (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-issues-airspace-notice-for-military-drills-near-strait-of-hormuz/3812508) and the January 25 - April 25, 2026 VFR (Visual Flight Rules) flights suspension which did not broadly close commercial aviation in a qualifying region (https://www.intellinews.com/iran-suspends-general-aviation-and-vfr-flights-in-new-airspace-directive-421997/).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Iran will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Iranian aviation authorities and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Amid heightened Middle East tensions following U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iranian military targets in late February—which triggered broad Tehran FIR closures—Iran's airspace partially reopened in April under a fragile ceasefire. On May 5, Iran launched missiles and drones toward the UAE, the first such attack since the truce, prompting a partial UAE airspace shutdown until May 11 and activating Iranian air defenses over Tehran. Traders weigh escalation risks, including potential Israeli or U.S. retaliation, proxy strikes, or further Iranian missile tests, against diplomatic de-escalation signals. No new broad NOTAM for commercial overflights has issued, but explosions reported in Iran yesterday signal ongoing volatility ahead of any resolution window.

eventMetadata.context_description: Gavin Newsom leads trader consensus at 26.4% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, reflecting his executive experience as California governor, national visibility as a vocal Trump administration critic, and strong early positioning amid high Polymarket volume exceeding $1 billion. Recent April polls, including a Politico survey showing him trouncing Kamala Harris in their home-state primary and a youth poll tying him atop Democratic preferences, bolster his edge over Harris (8.1%), whose 2024 general election loss lingers despite her April 10 statement musing about another White House bid at the National Action Network convention. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez matches Harris at 8.1% on progressive appeal and fundraising prowess but trails due to limited executive credentials. The fragmented field—featuring governors like Shapiro, Whitmer, and Pritzker—could consolidate via 2026 midterm successes, key endorsements, or early caucus polling in Iowa and New Hampshire, where swing-state executives hold advantages.

title: Bitcoin above ___ on May 5?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Binance 1 minute candle for BTC/USDT 12:00 in the ET timezone (noon) on the date specified in the title has a final "Close" price higher than the price specified in the title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Binance, specifically the BTC/USDT "Close" prices currently available at https://www.binance.com/en/trade/BTC_USDT with "1m" and "Candles" selected on the top bar.

Please note that this market is about the price according to Binance BTC/USDT, not according to other exchanges or trading pairs.

Price precision is determined by the number of decimal places in the source.

title: Elon Musk # tweets April 28 - May 5, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from April 28 12:00 PM ET to May 5, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". If the tracker does not update correctly in accordance with the rules, X itself may be used as a secondary resolution source.

eventMetadata.context_description: Polymarket trader consensus heavily favors Elon Musk posting 140-159 times on X from April 28 to May 5 (58% implied probability), with 160-179 close behind at 41%, driven by a live tally of 133 posts through six days elapsed—at a robust 22 daily average per XTracker data. Early sluggishness averaging 16 posts per day through May 2, tied to Musk's OpenAI trial court appearances, gave way to a surge matching late-April peaks like 22 on April 28 and 30-plus subsequently, amid X's record-high usage. With the market closing May 5 at noon ET, final-day posting pace amid potential viral controversies or platform buzz will decide if totals tip higher.

title: Next French Presidential Election
description:
The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects a tight race for France's 2027 presidential election, with Rassemblement National leader Jordan Bardella at 23.5% implied probability edging former Prime Minister Édouard Philippe of Horizons at 20.5%, driven by a fresh Ifop-Fiducial poll released May 4 showing Bardella as the most desired candidate at 44% versus Philippe's 36%. March municipal elections boosted far-right momentum with gains in cities like Nice, fueling anti-establishment sentiment, while Philippe's strong runoff polling against Bardella keeps him competitive in the two-round system. Jean-Luc Mélenchon's May 3 candidacy announcement lifted his odds to 8.5%, fragmenting the left. Separation could come from party primaries, economic shocks, or scandals before April 2027 voting.

title: Eurovision Winner 2026
description:
This market will resolve to the country whose candidate for Eurovision 2026 wins.

If at any point it is impossible for the listed candidate to win Eurovision 2026 based on the rules of the competition (i.e. they are eliminated), this market may immediately resolve to "No".

If no winner is announced by July 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve "Other". All ties will be broken according to EBU's official Eurovision rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Eurovision (https://eurovision.tv/), including live footage of Eurovision 2026, however a consensus of credible reporting will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: Finland's "Liekinheitin" by Linda Lampenius and Pete Parkkonen holds the frontrunner position at 35.4% implied probability on Polymarket, buoyed by its innovative string-heavy spectacle and broad appeal to both juries and televoters following a dominant UMK win and glowing pre-party reactions. Greece's Akylas with the upbeat "Ferto," fresh off victory in Sing For Greece, trails at 18.6% as a televote powerhouse, while Denmark's entry sits at 14.4% after slipping in recent pre-party assessments that questioned its top-tier contention. Australia's Delta Goodrem ("Eclipse") and France round out early challengers at 8.6% and 6.9%, respectively, with trader sentiment reflecting strong national final momentum and rehearsal buzz in Vienna. First rehearsals underway signal potential shifts ahead of semis on May 12 and 14, underscoring Eurovision's volatile jury-televote dynamics.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Oklahoma City Thunder hold home-court advantage in Game 1 of the Western Conference semifinals against the Los Angeles Lakers, fueled by their dominant regular-season sweep of LA (average margin of 29.3 points) and a first-round playoff sweep of the Suns. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's MVP-caliber play anchors OKC's offense, though Jalen Williams remains sidelined with a left hamstring strain from their series opener. The Lakers, resilient in a six-game upset over the Rockets, face major hurdles without Luka Doncic (out, left hamstring strain since early April with no firm return timeline), leaning heavily on LeBron James amid back-to-back road challenges and OKC's elite defense. Recent injury reports confirm these absences, shaping a lopsided trader consensus.

markets.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $150 in May?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation during May 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours. 

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract’s last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract’s last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date.

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation during May 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours. 

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract’s last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract’s last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date.

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

eventMetadata.context_description: WTI crude oil spot prices have retreated over 3% to approximately $102 per barrel as of May 5, 2026, down from Monday's 2026 highs above $105, as traders digest OPEC+'s May 3 announcement to raise production quotas by 188,000 barrels per day starting June—signaling ample supply amid softening global demand from China and building U.S. inventories. Backwardation in the futures curve reflects near-term tightness from Middle East tensions, including Strait of Hormuz risks, but longer-dated contracts price in downward pressure from increased non-OPEC output. Polymarket traders' skin-in-the-game consensus hinges on EIA's weekly petroleum status report due this week, with potential inventory builds capping upside, while the IEA's May Oil Market Report and June 7 OPEC+ review loom as key catalysts for May price extremes.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: A fragile ceasefire brokered by Pakistan has held since April 8 amid the 2026 Iran war, but US-Iran indirect negotiations remain stalled after marathon Islamabad talks collapsed on April 12 over Iran's refusal to commit against nuclear weapons development, prompting a US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump rejected Tehran's latest 14-point proposal on May 1, deeming it unsatisfactory on nuclear curbs, sanctions relief, and regional security guarantees, while recent incidents—Iranian forces firing on US ships, met with retaliatory strikes—highlight ongoing tensions. US envoy Steve Witkoff indicated resumed conversations as of May 3, with Iran reviewing a US response, though Trump signaled likely rejection; traders anticipate protracted diplomacy given these sticking points and historical negotiation patterns.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent naval clashes in the Strait of Hormuz, including Iranian missile strikes on U.S. vessels and American helicopter fire on fast boats, have tested the fragile April ceasefire following U.S. and Israeli airstrikes on Iranian nuclear and missile sites earlier this year, yet traders see low odds of a full-scale U.S. ground invasion before 2027. President Trump is reviewing Tehran's multi-phase counterproposal for ending hostilities—calling for lifted sanctions, naval blockade removal, and non-aggression guarantees—while announcing U.S. Navy escorts for commercial shipping to reopen the strait amid economic pressures. Saudi Arabia urged de-escalation, and no official plans for troop deployments signaling invasion have emerged, reflecting war fatigue after Iraq and Afghanistan alongside diplomatic maneuvering.

title: LoL: Dplus KIA vs Nongshim Red Force (BO3) - Esports World Cup Korea Qualifier Playoffs
description:
This market refers to the LoL Upper bracket quarterfinal 2 match between Dplus KIA and Nongshim Red Force in the Esports World Cup Korea Qualifier Playoffs, initially scheduled for May 4 at 7:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to "Dplus KIA" if Dplus KIA win the match against Nongshim Red Force.

This market will resolve to "Nongshim Red Force" if Nongshim Red Force win the match against Dplus KIA.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Dplus KIA and Nongshim Red Force each slay Baron Nashor at least once during Game 1. This market will resolve to "No" if either team (or both teams) does not slay Baron Nashor during Game 1.

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 is never played due to forfeit, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 is remade, resolution will be based on the remade game only.

eventMetadata.context_description: Dplus KIA holds a clear edge in the Esports World Cup 2026 Korea Qualifier playoffs BO3 upper bracket matchup against Nongshim RedForce, fueled by stronger LCK 2026 Rounds 1-2 form at 6-4 overall (5th place, +5 map differential) versus NS's struggling 4-6 record (6th, -4 maps, four-match losing streak). Historical head-to-head dominance sees DK winning 82% of 28 prior series, including recent LCK encounters. DK's stable roster—featuring top laner Siwoo, jungler Lucid, mid laner ShowMaker, ADC Smash, and support Career—contrasts NS's recent bot lane shakeup with new ADC Diable via trade. No confirmed injuries or absences; both teams adapt to the latest patch amid tight LCK scheduling, with a DK win advancing them toward Hanwha Life Esports in Round 2.

title: Russia x Ukraine ceasefire by May 31, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement, between Russia and Ukraine by May 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the ceasefire officially starts afterward.

Only ceasefires which constitute a general pause in the conflict will qualify. Ceasefires which only apply to energy infrastructure, the Black Sea, or other similar agreements will not qualify.

Any form of informal agreement will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses will not count toward the resolution of this market.

A peace deal or political framework will qualify if it includes a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement, effective on a specific date. Frameworks or agreements that outline terms for a future peace but do not include an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not count.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a wide consensus of credible media reporting stating an official ceasefire agreement between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire by May 31 at just 6.3%, reflecting entrenched military escalation and stalled diplomacy despite recent short-term truce gestures. On May 4, President Putin declared a unilateral two-day pause for May 8-9 Victory Day celebrations, prompting President Zelenskyy to announce a rival halt starting midnight May 5-6 to preempt violations and expose insincerity. Prior Easter and other brief cessations saw mutual accusations of breaches amid ongoing drone strikes, with Ukraine hitting Russian oil facilities causing environmental fallout and Russia suffering its first net territorial loss since mid-2023 in April. Absent comprehensive talks or de-escalation signals, traders see formidable barriers to resolution before month's end, though U.S.-brokered feelers via Trump persist.

title: Elon Musk # tweets May 1 - May 8, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from May 1 12:00 PM ET to May 8, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by May 15?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and May 15, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for May 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices "No" at 97.8% for Strait of Hormuz traffic returning to normal by May 15, driven by over two months of dual blockades amid the US-Iran war: Iran enforces restrictions via sea mines, drone and boat attacks since February 28, 2026, while US naval operations block Iranian ports. Commercial transits remain at 10-20% of the 60-ship daily baseline, with 250 vessels stranded and war-risk insurance at six times normal levels. Recent US Project Freedom escorts enabled just two merchant ships to pass on May 4 amid clashes, including US sinking of Iranian boats and Iranian strikes on UAE oil facilities, underscoring fragile ceasefire risks. Only a major diplomatic breakthrough or de-escalation enabling unescorted flows could shift odds in the next 10 days.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President JD Vance holds a slim lead in trader consensus at 20% implied probability to win the 2028 presidential election, closely pursued by California Governor Gavin Newsom at 17% and Secretary of State Marco Rubio at 10%, underscoring the fluid dynamics of an open Republican succession post-Trump and a fragmented Democratic field. Vance's edge stems from vice presidential incumbency, early 2026 Iowa visits signaling primary groundwork, and locked-in GOP support, though recent diplomatic snubs—like Rubio's selection for a papal meeting amid Iran war tensions—have fueled Rubio's surge via foreign policy visibility from Venezuela strikes and Middle East escalations. Newsom leads Democratic nominee markets with over $1 billion in volume, buoyed by his national profile. The 2026 midterms, potential Trump endorsements, and scandals could widen gaps in this closely contested race.

title: Fed Decision in June?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's June 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for June 16-17, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their June meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices a 95.5% implied probability of no Federal Reserve rate change at the June 2026 FOMC meeting, reflecting sticky inflation and labor market resilience after March CPI surged 0.9% month-over-month to 3.3% annually—its highest since May 2024—fueled by energy shocks amid geopolitical tensions. The Fed's April 29 decision to hold the federal funds rate at 3.50%-3.75% amid internal dissent, coupled with Chair Powell's data-dependent remarks emphasizing persistent price pressures over cuts, has solidified higher-for-longer expectations, aligning with the March dot plot's median end-2026 rate near 3.4%. April nonfarm payrolls and the May 12 CPI release loom as key catalysts, though a sharp labor market downturn or sub-3% inflation print could challenge this positioning.

title: F1 Drivers' Champion
description:
This market will resolve according to the listed driver that finishes 1st in the driver standings for the 2026 F1 season.

This market will resolve as soon as the official results of the final scheduled race of the 2026 F1 season are known.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

title: Will the Iranian regime fall by May 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran’s current ruling regime is overthrown, collapsed, or otherwise ceases to govern by May 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This requires a broad consensus of reporting indicating that core structures of the Islamic Republic (e.g. the office of the Supreme Leader, the Guardian Council, IRGC control under clerical authority) have been dissolved, incapacitated, or replaced by a fundamentally different governing system or otherwise lost de facto power over a majority of the population of Iran. This could occur via revolution, civil war, military coup, or voluntary abdication, but only qualifies if the Islamic Republic no longer exercises sovereign power.

Routine political events such as elections, reforms, or leadership succession do not qualify. Internal coups or power shifts that preserve the Islamic Republic’s core structures also do not qualify. Only a clear break in continuity—such as a new provisional government, revolutionary council, or constitution replacing the Islamic Republic will qualify.

Partial loss of territory or challenges from rebel or exile groups will not qualify unless the Islamic Republic no longer administers the majority of the Iranian population within Iran. 

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: The top-seeded Detroit Pistons (60-22) host the fourth-seeded Cleveland Cavaliers (52-30) in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference semifinals at Little Caesars Arena, both teams advancing via grueling Game 7 first-round triumphs within the past 48 hours. Detroit's remarkable rally from a 3-1 deficit against Orlando—capped by Cade Cunningham's 32 points and 12 assists in a 116-94 rout—bolsters their momentum and home-court edge for Games 1 and 2, while Cleveland outlasted Toronto behind Donovan Mitchell's scoring punch. With clean injury reports and a regular-season series split 2-2, short rest, backcourt matchups between Cunningham and Mitchell, and playoff experience define trader consensus on this evenly poised clash.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if both HANJIN BRION Challengers and Gen.G Global Academy each slay Baron Nashor at least once during Game 3. This market will resolve to "No" if either team (or both teams) does not slay Baron Nashor during Game 3.

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 3 is never played due to forfeit, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 3 is not played because the series result has already been determined (e.g., a team clinches the series before Game 3 is needed), this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 3 begins but is not completed and ends via surrender, this market will resolve based on whether both teams had slain Baron Nashor prior to stoppage. If the condition was not met, this market will resolve to "No".

If Game 3 is remade, resolution will be based on the remade game only.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

markets.question: Game 3: Odd/Even Total Kills?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Odd" if the total combined kills by both teams in Game 3 is an odd number.

This market will resolve to "Even" if the total combined kills by both teams in Game 3 is an even number.

"Total combined kills" includes all champion kills recorded during the match by both HANJIN BRION Challengers and Gen.G Global Academy. Executions (deaths to non-champion sources such as turrets, minions, or neutral monsters where no enemy champion receives kill credit) do not count as kills for the purposes of this market.

If no kills are recorded in Game 3, or if Game 3 is canceled (not played at all) or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date, this market will resolve to 50-50.

eventMetadata.context_description: HANJIN BRION Challengers enter their Week 6 BO3 rematch against Gen.G Global Academy with a slight edge in LCK Challengers League Rounds 1-2 standings, holding a 3-7 series record (9-15 games) for 8th place versus Gen.G's 2-8 (8-17 games) and last-place position. BRION's 2-1 head-to-head win over Gen.G in Week 2 (April 2) underscores their matchup advantage, amid both academy teams' bottom-table struggles in the double round-robin format. Recent form shows BRION securing late-April map wins on blue side after losses to Nongshim and DN SOOPers Challengers, while Gen.G extends a four-series skid; no roster changes noted ahead of today's contest on patch 26.08, keeping focus on execution in this pivotal survival matchup.

title: Will Trump visit China by...?
description:
If U.S. President Donald Trump visits China by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial or maritime territory of the listed country. Whether or not Trump enters the country's airspace during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: President Trump's planned state visit to China on May 14-15 for a summit with President Xi Jinping drives current trader consensus, following a postponement from late March due to the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz security concerns. Trump recently reaffirmed the trip will proceed as scheduled—calling it "amazing"—despite stalemated Iran peace talks, with White House confirmations and Beijing preparations underscoring diplomatic momentum to stabilize bilateral relations amid trade tensions, rare earths supply, and tariff disputes. No further delays have materialized in the past week, though Iran escalations or domestic priorities could still impact execution; a reciprocal Xi visit to Washington is anticipated later in 2026.
